groups.text: It is currently 16 degrees and cloudy in Berlin-Tempelhof.
With the morning weather set, here is the news.

Pop star Taylor Swift and American football player Travis Kelce have married in New York City. A spokesperson for the singer confirmed the news Friday following weeks of speculation. The couple held a large-scale event at Madison Square Garden where comedian Adam Sandler officiated the ceremony. Austin Swift and Jason Kelce served as witnesses, while the pair wore designs by Christian Dior and Jonathan Anderson with shoes by Christian Louboutin and jewelry from Cartier. Separately, Mistral AI has released Leanstral 1.5, an open-source model designed for formal verification in the Lean 4 programming language. The model achieved a perfect score on the miniF2F math benchmark and solved 587 of 672 problems on PutnamBench. Beyond mathematics, the tool demonstrated its utility in code verification by scanning 57 open-source repositories and identifying five previously unknown bugs, including an overflow bug within the Rust library varinteger.

The General Staff of the Armed Forces of Ukraine reports that Russia has lost over 1.4 million troops since the full-scale invasion began in February 2022. This total includes 1,190 casualties suffered over the past day alone. Russian losses also extend to heavy equipment, including more than 12,000 tanks and 45,000 artillery systems. In Russia, a fire broke out Saturday at the St. Petersburg Oil Terminal, a strategic site for crude oil transshipment. Local officials claimed air defenses downed 67 drones over the region, though OSINT analysis suggests a railway tank car may have been burning on nearby tracks. While these conflicts persist in Europe, the focus shifts to Philadelphia Stadium today. France and Paraguay meet at 5 p.m. for the World Cup Round of 16. Kylian Mbappe’s France enters as the favorite, seeking a path toward their third World Cup title.

Official mourning has begun in Iran for the long-time leader Ali Chamenei, who was killed during U.S. and Israeli airstrikes in February. Millions of people are expected to attend the six-day ceremonies in Tehran before his burial this Thursday in Maschhad. In Germany, police have partially closed the A71 motorway due to security concerns surrounding an AfD party congress in Erfurt. Authorities expect roughly 50,000 counter-demonstrators and over 30 registered assemblies to protest the gathering. Meanwhile, Turkey has published a presidential circular establishing a National Green Finance Strategy and Action Plan for 2026 through 2029 to support the country's green transformation. In a different vein, Scotland is seeing a surge in the practice of placing traffic cones on statues. This trend follows the Tartan Army doing the same to monuments in Boston during the World Cup, extending a tradition previously centered on the Duke of Wellington statue in Glasgow.

Ethiopia is breaking ground on the Bishoftu International Airport, a twelve-point-seven billion dollar project designed to make the country the largest aviation hub in Africa. Located forty kilometers southeast of Addis Ababa, the massive site will cover thirty-five square kilometers to support the growth ambitions of Ethiopian Airlines. In Germany, physicists at the University of Paderborn have achieved a different kind of breakthrough. Led by Lorenzo Procopio and published in Nature, the team used ultra-fast laser pulses in optical fibers to observe an analogue of Hawking radiation backreaction for the first time. This simulates how black holes lose energy through radiation, a process that remains impossible to observe directly in space. Meanwhile, German domestic debate is heating up over proposed government rules for sick leave. The administration plans to require medical certificates from the first day of illness rather than the fourth, sparking criticism from some newspapers over increased burdens on rural patients.

In Ankara, municipal workers are planting flowers and installing giant billboards to hide dilapidated homes ahead of a high-stakes Nato summit beginning Tuesday. The facelift aims to burnish the city's image for thirty-two heads of state, including US President Donald Trump, but strict security measures and road closures have drawn sharp criticism from locals and opposition politicians. Meanwhile, in Southeast Asia, Vietnam and the U.S. held their 173rd repatriation ceremony on July 2nd for the possible remains of a service member missing in action during the Vietnam War. Shifting to software, PyTorch developers have released a fix for their pack analyzer. The update addresses an issue where analysis failed when a predicate was lane uniform, a problem discovered while reviewing attention-gym. These three events share no direct link, reflecting a morning of disparate geopolitical efforts and technical refinements.

In Tehran, thousands of followers have gathered for the official public homage to Supreme Leader Ali Khamenei. These national funerals serve as a demonstration of force following the war against Israel and the United States. This conflict with Iran is now a central point of tension for NATO Secretary-General Mark Rutte, who is working to keep Donald Trump engaged with the alliance. Ahead of a July 7 summit in Ankara, Rutte has used gold-colored display boards to highlight that European allies and Canada have increased defense spending by 1.2 trillion dollars since 2017. While global security remains strained, New York saw a different kind of lockdown this weekend. Pop star Taylor Swift and NFL player Travis Kelce married at Madison Square Garden during the United States' 250th birthday. The couple avoided public announcements and reportedly required guests to sign non-disclosure agreements for the ceremony.

An intense heat dome has gripped the center and east of the United States, forcing the cancellation of dozens of Fourth of July celebrations. In Washington, temperatures hitting 38 degrees Celsius led to the temporary closure of the Great American State Fair, while a projected heat index of 46 degrees Celsius forced the National Park Service to cancel its Independence Day parade. The extreme weather has strained electrical grids and triggered alerts for over half the U.S. population. Meanwhile, in India, GoDaddy is challenging a Delhi High Court order that ends default privacy for domain owners, arguing that requiring e-KYC and disclosing registrant details exposes users to harassment. A larger bench will hear these appeals on July 16. In Europe, President Volodymyr Zelenskyy announced that the Netherlands has agreed to host a Special Tribunal for the Crime of Aggression against Ukraine to hold Russia's leadership accountable.
After the headlines, back to the weather.
This afternoon will be cloudy with temperatures between 18 and 21 degrees.
And from the weather, a quick look at the calendar.
And that's it for your personal morning broadcast.
[mature adult voice, intensely emotional, tender, radiant; hold a long breath after Rise] Rise... and shine.
[very very long pause before speaking; then mature adult voice, most emotional, strong, warm, radiant, deeply encouraging; hold a long breath after Rise] Rise... and shine.
